papers.title: Finding and using interpretable latents in a neutrino foundation model with sparse autoencoders
papers.abstract: We present a first application of sparse-autoencoder-based mechanistic interpretability to particle physics. Studying a neutrino foundation model pretrained on IceCube data and fine-tuned for direction reconstruction, we identify a validated atlas of physical concepts in the model representation, using a strict validation protocol consisting of held-out tests, matched nuisance controls, and replication across independent dictionary trainings. Causal interventions show that the direction head barely draws on this atlas. Motivated by this underused information, we train an uncertainty head on the same event-level representation to predict the model's angular reconstruction error. Unlike the direction head, it depends causally on quality and brightness features from the atlas. These results suggest that mechanistic interpretability can reveal learned latent physics encoded within a model's internal representation and help design downstream tasks that exploit it.

papers.title: Unlocking Pandora's Secrets: Probing the Thermodynamics of Abell 2744
papers.abstract: Abell 2744 (Pandora's Cluster) is a massive galaxy cluster undergoing multiple mergers, characterized by a highly disturbed X-ray morphology, elevated intracluster medium (ICM) temperatures, and several radio relics associated with merger driven shocks. We present NuSTAR observations of Abell 2744 aimed at mapping its thermodynamic structure and constraining the presence of inverse Compton (IC) scattering from relativistic electrons. We measure the temperature distribution across the cluster and identify a prominent shock front with a Mach number of $\mathcal{M} = 1.58^{+0.42}_{-0.30}$, aligning with the southeastern boundary of the radio halo. The global NuSTAR spectra are modeled with single- and two-temperature thermal components, as well as thermal plus power-law models to test for IC emission. The spectra are well described by purely thermal models with an average temperature of $kT \approx 11$ keV, and we find no significant evidence for non-thermal hard X-ray emission. We derive a 90\% confidence upper limit on the $20-80$ keV IC flux of $ F_{\rm nt} < 2.31 \times 10^{-12} erg~s^{-1}~cm^{-2}$. Combining this with 1.5 GHz diffuse radio measurements from the VLA, we estimate a lower limit on the average magnetic field strength of $B > 0.2 \ \rm{\mu G}$.

papers.title: A Sub-Parsec Origin for Rapid Accretion-State Transitions in Radio-Loud AGN
papers.abstract: I investigate the physical origin and timescale of accretion-state transitions in radio-loud active galactic nuclei, focusing on the evolution from FRII high-excitation radio galaxies (HERGs) to FRII low-excitation radio galaxies (LERGs) within the framework of Garofalo, Evans & Sambruna (2010). I show that the required transition timescale of about 4 million yr arises naturally if the accretion rate is regulated at sub-parsec radii (about 0.1-0.3 pc), corresponding to viscous evolution at about one thousand to ten thousand R_g for black hole masses 100 million to 1 billion solar masses. These radii coincide with the broad-line region and inner dusty torus, where multiphase gas dynamics regulate the effective inward mass flux on Myr timescales. I argue that powerful FRII jet feedback heats and perturbs the surrounding medium, reducing the effective mass supply reaching the inner disk. Once the accretion rate falls below the critical threshold m_crit about 0.01, the inner flow rapidly transitions to an advection-dominated accretion flow (ADAF). Observations of molecular gas reservoirs in radio galaxies are compatible with this picture because the transition requires suppression of inward fueling rather than complete removal of cold gas. I conclude that rapid, internally driven evolution provides a physically consistent basis for the FRII HERG -> FRII LERG transition while linking radio morphology, accretion state, and cosmic evolution.

papers.title: Hydrodynamic Natal Kicks and Formation of Black Hole Binaries
papers.abstract: The observation of over 300 Gravitational Wave (GW) events by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaboration, has yielded information of the merger of compact object binaries, such as their individual masses and spins. However, the effective spin parameter obtained from the GW signal provides important information that could be used to discern the binary's formation channel. Overall, binaries formed from dynamic interactions in dense stellar environments are expected to have a random distribution of effective spins between -1 and 1. Meanwhile, binaries formed from the evolution of isolated stellar binaries are expected to have positive effective spins unless there is a large enough natal kick during the compact object formation that could significantly alter the orientation of the individual spins with respect to the binary's angular momentum. We study the viability of obtaining large natal kicks during the formation of massive Black Holes by studying the asymmetric mild explosion of $13\text{M}_{\odot}$, $21\text{M}_{\odot}$, $28\text{M}_{\odot}$ and $34\text{M}_{\odot}$ pre-supernova stellar models, by means of 3D Smooth Particle Hydrodynamics simulations. Our results show that, even kicks in the order of $\sim$ 1000 km/s, which are among the highest values observed for natal kicks, can't consistently change the orientation of the orbit. Physical setups where the orientation of the orbit changes require the kick to be directed correctly, and they would also require for the supernova explosion energy to be quite high.

papers.title: Testing influence of tides on gravitational wave emission with SPH code PHANTOM
papers.abstract: In this article, we demonstrate how a Newtonian SPH (Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics) code PHANTOM can be used to estimate the tidal contribution to gravitational wave (GW) waveforms. Using a binary neutron star (NS+NS) system with typical masses of 1.5 + 1.5 Msun as an example, we show - by comparing our results with waveforms calibrated against full numerical General Relativity (GR) simulations - that the tidal contribution to GWs can be reliably extracted using as few as about 10$^4$ smoothed particles. Naturally, one must account for the difference in neutron star compactness between Newtonian gravity and general relativity. At separations greater than 100 km, the relative tidal contribution falls below the level of numerical noise inherent in SPH; however, at such distances, GW waveforms for point-like sources are sufficient for detection purposes. For a white dwarf-neutron star (WD+NS) binary with typical masses of 0.6 Msun and 1.5 Msun respectively, a much larger number of smoothed particles is required, along with a separation on the order of tens of thousands of kilometers, as tidal mass transfer and the disruption of the white dwarf begin quite rapidly. Nevertheless, these challenges can be overcome, but the approach is not capable of yielding useful results due to the richness of Newtonian effects. In all cases, it is crucial to perform a hydrostatic/hydrodynamic relaxation (HPR) of the initial models; otherwise, the entire GW signal is lost in the numerical noise.

papers.title: Neutrino pair annihilation in curved spacetime: a fast moment method and the geometry of flavour conversion
papers.abstract: Neutrino-antineutrino annihilation above black-hole accretion discs is shaped both by general-relativistic transport and by neutrino flavour conversion. Whether these effects can be treated independently depends on how gravity weights the different flavour populations. We investigate this interplay using backward ray tracing in Schwarzschild and Kerr spacetimes, combined with an exact angular-moment formulation of the annihilation kernel that we validate against the analytic spherical solution and published disc calculations. We first establish that flavour-conversion corrections are independent of the spacetime geometry when conversion is uniform and the initial heavy-lepton neutrino emission is negligible. For uniform conversion, this separability remains approximately valid when the flavour-dependent emitting regions overlap: compared with the same discs in flat space, moving with the same local velocities, gravity enhances the deposited energy by factors of 1.4-5, while changing the relative conversion effect by no more than 6% for most temperature profiles considered; conversion that varies across the disc raises this to 22% around a rapidly spinning hole. A qualitatively different regime emerges when heavy-lepton neutrinos originate from an inner ring separated from the electron-flavour emitting regions. Relativistic bending and energy shifts preferentially enhance annihilations involving inner-ring neutrinos, producing relativistic conversion factors up to 2.4 times the flat-space ones. In one configuration, flavour equipartition reduces the deposition by 54% in flat space but increases it by 11% in Kerr spacetime. These results identify the spatial arrangement of flavour-dependent neutrinospheres as a key determinant, in the models considered, of whether flavour conversion and relativistic transport can be treated separately.

papers.title: Bicoherence States from QPO-Accretion Flow Coupling in Black Hole X-ray Binaries
papers.abstract: We calculate the bispectrum of a black hole X-ray binary light curve model where lognormal fluctuations associated with the inner flow are multiplicatively modulated by a quasi-periodic oscillation (QPO) and its harmonic. The bispectrum is a third-order Fourier statistic which measures the strength of nonlinear relationships between frequencies in a timeseries. When applied to black hole X-ray binaries, the bispectrum reveals nonlinear coupling between QPOs and the broadband noise. These couplings are sorted into a small set of states and X-ray binaries are observed to transition between these states as they undergo spectral transitions. We show that the model we consider is able to reproduce all of the canonical bispectral states analytically. We consider other sources of incoherent variability which dilute this model light curve and find that changes in this dilution, together with changes in the QPO amplitude, drive the transitions between the bispectral states. We also show that the larger QPO amplitudes of high-inclination sources favor the cross state and the weaker QPOs of low-inclination sources favor the hypotenuse state, which can explain the empirically observed correlation. Additionally, any dilution by equatorial winds, which are seen mainly at high inclination, would push high-inclination sources further toward the cross state.

papers.title: Modeling of the X-ray Flux and Polarization Energy Spectra of Black Hole X-Ray Binaries with the KerrC Code
papers.abstract: In this chapter, we introduce the kerrC model, an advanced framework designed for the analysis of combined spectral and polarimetric X-ray emission from black hole systems. The model is built upon an extensive dataset of ray-tracing Monte Carlo simulations that compute the radiative transfer of X-rays in the strongly curved spacetime near the event horizon of a Kerr black hole. These simulations incorporate thermal seed emission from a geometrically thin, optically thick accretion disk, along with the subsequent Comptonization processes within a hot corona of variable geometry and physical properties. Crucially, the reflection of both primary disk and Comptonized photons is treated self-consistently utilizing the xillver reflection tables, and the polarization 4-vectors of the photons are rigorously transported throughout the simulation to preserve full polarization information. The code tracks photons forward in time, allowing for multiple photon scatterings in the corona and off the accretion disk. We detail the underlying mechanics of the ray-tracing simulations and the fitting models, and discuss the applications of kerrC in leveraging X-ray polarization observations to constrain black hole spin and coronal geometry.

papers.title: Dynamical formation of Gaia neutron star binaries in star clusters as a phase-dependent process
papers.abstract: Gaia has discovered dormant compact-object binaries in which the compact object shows no observable interaction with its luminous companion. These systems, hereafter Gaia BHs and Gaia NSs for black hole (BH) and neutron star (NS) companions, provide a new probe of compact-object binary formation. These detached systems are difficult to produce through standard isolated binary evolution alone, and their formation pathways remain unclear. Previous $N$-body studies have shown that Gaia BH-like objects are formed efficiently in star clusters, while Gaia NS-like objects are not. This has been attributed to the BH subsystem dominating the cluster core. We performed direct $N$-body simulations of $10^4 \mathrm{M}_\odot$ star clusters in a Galactic tidal field and investigated how NS-main-sequence (NS-MS) binaries form during the late BH-depleted phase. We found that NS-MS binaries satisfying Gaia-sensitive criteria form only after BH depletion. NSs are present in the core throughout the evolution, but the strong encounters there are monopolized by the BH subsystem until it is depleted. Our results show that the dynamical formation of Gaia-sensitive NS-MS systems is not prevented in star clusters, but delayed relative to Gaia BH-like systems.

papers.title: Probing Dark Matter via the Migdal Effect in LUX-ZEPLIN Data
papers.abstract: Sub-GeV dark matter (DM) particles deposit little energy in conventional direct-detection experiments and are therefore difficult to probe, but the Migdal effect provides an electronic signal from atomic ionization accompanying the recoil. Using the new results of the LUX-ZEPLIN experiment with a 4.2 tonne-year exposure, we evaluate the sensitivity of the Migdal effect to the spin-independent DM--nucleon scattering cross section. For masses between $350~\mathrm{MeV}$ and $10~\mathrm{GeV}$, the projected 90\% upper limits range from $6.5\times10^{-37}$ to $9.6\times10^{-42}~\mathrm{cm^2}$. These limits are then used to constrain the minimal scalar- and vector-mediator DM models. For the light-mediator DM model, the constraint on the coupling reaches $\alpha\simeq 10^{-12}$, which is stronger than or comparable to the constraints from kaon decays, stellar cooling, and SN1987A.

papers.title: Quasi-spherical fallback in binary neutron-star mergers: fuel and obstacle for extended emission
papers.abstract: Extended emission (EE) lasting hundreds of seconds has been observed in a fraction of short gamma-ray bursts (sGRB) containing both nonthermal and thermal components, and representing a significant puzzle for models involving binary neutron stars (BNSs). Recent GRMHD simulations of BNS mergers found that the late-time fallback is approximately quasi-spherical and motivated an r-process powered thermal model for EE. However, the available radioactive-heating power may be insufficient to sustain the luminosity inferred by such a model. We therefore propose a fallback-fed secondary-jet scenario in which a fraction of the fallback material circularizes on the black-hole equatorial plane and powers the jet, while polar fallback impedes its propagation. Using a semi-analytic toy model, we follow the propagation of the jet-head through the fallback envelope and identify jet-dominated, cocoon-dominated, and choked scenarios. The boundaries of these regimes depend primarily on the circularization fraction $f_{\rm circ}$, on the jet half-opening angle $\theta_j$, and on the polar refilling factor $\xi_{\rm pol}$, with the approximate scaling $\widetilde{L}\propto f_{\rm circ}/(\xi_{\rm pol}\theta_j^2)$. By post-processing data from BNS-merger simulations we find that the fraction of bound fallback material that avoids prompt capture is $f_{\rm npc}\simeq0.52$, thus providing an upper bound on the circularizable fallback supply. Under suitable prescriptions for nonthermal jet emission and thermal emission from the jet head, the estimated isotropic-equivalent $0.3$--$10$ keV energies reproduce well both the observed EE distribution for the jet-dominated branch and its low-energy end for the cocoon-dominated branch. Overall, these results suggest that fallback-fed secondary jets represent a dynamically feasible and energetically consistent explanation of the EE in sGRBs.

papers.title: GW230729\_082317 and GW231118\_005626: A Candidate of Hierarchical Triple Mergers
papers.abstract: Hierarchical triple mergers denote a sequential merger process in which the black hole remnant from an initial binary merger subsequently merges with a third black hole. In this study, we identify a related pair of binary black hole mergers, GW230729\_082317 and GW231118\_005626, which exhibit consistent sky localization and luminosity distances; the latter is identified as a candidate hierarchical merger binary back holes. The Bayes factor in favor of a hierarchical triple merger origin over the non-association hypothesis is $110$. However, after accounting for the priors odds, the corresponding odds ratio decreases to $0.1$, indicating that the current evidence is insufficient to favor the hierarchical triple merger scenario. GW230720\_0823 show no detectable signatures of orbit eccentricity or line-of-sight acceleration. The inferred properties of these two gravitational wave events suggest a dynamical formation channel, such as few-body scattering or gas-assisted mergers, while a primordial triple origin is disfavored. Among the proposed dynamical environments, the accretion disk of an active galactic nucleus provides the most plausible site. We further derive constraints on the local rate of hierarchical triple mergers rate under both the null and candidate scenarios. Under the assumption of no detected hierarchical triple mergers, the most stringent $90\%$ confidence upper limit is $4.2\,{\rm Gpc^{-3}yr^{-1}}$ for $t_{\rm max}=10$ years using the GWTC-4 catalog.

papers.title: Activity of the ejected galactic nuclei and cosmic rays
papers.abstract: The double and triple approaches of supermassive central black holes are a fairly common process in the hierarchical picture of galaxy formation. In this case, the ejection of a black hole is possible; it may carry the accretion disk and some amount of stars with it. The activity of the galactic nucleus can be restored after the ejection. One consequence of this activity is an ultrafast gas outflow, accompanied by a shock wave. We show that the acceleration of cosmic rays at such a shock is more effective than in the case of a stationary galactic nucleus due to the lower density of the surrounding gas and the higher velocity of the shock front. In this case, proton acceleration can occur up to energies of ~10^{19} eV, which is an order of magnitude higher than in an ordinary nucleus in the centers of galaxies.

papers.title: Constraints on Cosmic-Rays and the MeV Emission from Jupiter's Atmosphere
papers.abstract: The Cosmic $\gamma$-ray Background (CGB) in the MeV regime remains among the least understood components of diffuse cosmic radiation, primarily due to instrumental limitations in detecting faint isotropic emission at MeV energies. We present an indirect method for probing isotropic emission from soft X-rays to $\gamma$-rays through scattered emission in Jupiter's atmosphere. Using archival observations from SPI, the spectrometer aboard INTEGRAL, spanning 22 years of serendipitous Jupiter observations, we analyse the planet as a moving $\gamma$-ray point source in the 30 keV to 8 MeV range. Our analysis focuses on Jupiter's $\gamma$-ray albedo, produced by high-energy photon and cosmic-ray interactions. We performed detailed Monte Carlo simulations to model the response of Jupiter's atmosphere to incident photons, protons, electrons, positrons, and alpha particles. We simulate a 1000 km deep spherical atmosphere with 1 km shell resolution, based on Galileo probe measurements. By comparing empirical and astrophysical models with the SPI data, we find no statistically significant emission from Jupiter. We derive $2\sigma$ upper limits across the 30 keV to 8 MeV band, which we compare with cutoff power-law, reflected CGB, cosmic-ray-induced, and long-lived mediator dark matter models. We constrain Jupiter's bremsstrahlung luminosity in the MeV range to $10^{18}$ erg/s, close to that inferred from in situ measurements obtained by Juno/JEDI. While the expected emission from the CGB and cosmic rays is a factor of $10^4$ and 100 below our upper limits, respectively, this work establishes planetary atmospheres as promising indirect probes of diffuse $\gamma$-ray backgrounds for future MeV missions.

papers.title: XMM-Newton observations of the highest field polar AR UMa: An extreme case of soft-blobby accretion
papers.abstract: (Context) The X-ray spectra of magnetic cataclysmic variables (MCVs) with extreme magnetic fields, the polars, often exhibit a prominent soft X-ray excess attributed to buried shocks. (Aims) Using the first-ever high-state XMM-Newton observation of the highest field polar, AR UMa ($B\approx230$ MG), we established the source's accretion scenario and derived the energy budget at the magnetic extreme of MCVs. (Methods) Using X-ray, UV, and optical spectral and timing analysis, we disentangled the radiation components and located their origin in the binary. (Results) AR UMa showed one active ("southern") pole during our observation. The spectrum of the active pole was dominated by soft, blackbody-like emission with $kT_{\rm BB} \simeq 35$ eV and showed no evidence for an optically thin hard X-ray emission characteristic of a cooling post-shock accretion column. Instead, we find constant, faint, optically thin plasma emission with a temperature of $\approx 1$ keV at all orbital phases, which is uncorrelated with the soft X-ray emission, and we attribute this to shock-heated matter at the stagnation region. Pronounced absorption dips punctuate the phase of active X-ray emission and are associated with puffed-up material in the stagnation region. Using spectro-timing analysis of the absorption dips, the density profile and evolution of the clumpy flow were probed. We find evidence of a cyclotron harmonic from the southern pole (160 MG) near $\sim$2300 Angstrom in the UV spectrum. We report minute-long quasi-periodic oscillations in the optical, UV, and X-ray light curves. (Conclusion) AR UMa represents an extreme case of soft, blobby accretion, with an effectively infinite soft excess, extending the magnetic field range over which magnetic accretion can be studied by a factor of two. It is one of the rare systems in which X-ray emission from a stream-magnetosphere interaction is detected.

papers.title: Fundamental Noise Processes in Pulsar Timing
papers.abstract: The stability of spin rates and emission regions of radio-emitting neutron stars (pulsars) has enabled remarkable advances, including the detection of exoplanets, testing theories of gravity, and stimulating the vigorous exploration of a new window in gravitational wave astronomy an nanohertz frequencies. An ideal astrophysical clock would emit identical pulses at a constant rate, propagating along single geodesics through a perfect vacuum. In reality, the timing precision achievable with pulsars is limited by spin noise, variability in the beam produced in a complex magnetosphere, and multipath propagation through a turbulent interstellar medium, with additional limitations from uncertainties in the changing pulsar -- observatory vector and instrumental effects. Here we present the fundamentals of pulsar timing, its current limitations, and prospects for improvements in timing precision. We develop metrics to assess the timing quality of a pulsar and use them to evaluate sources currently included in pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) as a means for characterizing the quality of future pulsar discoveries. With increases in telescope sensitivity, pulsar timing precision will increasingly be limited by propagation effects in the interstellar medium. We identify sources of non-Gaussianity in timing residuals and separate out effects that are chromatic or achromatic, as well as effects that vary on short (seconds to minutes) and longer (days to months) timescales. Modern wide-bandwidth receivers provide simultaneous arrival times across a range of frequencies, enabling the robust mitigation of chromatic interstellar effects and the identification of non-Gaussian events superimposed on random fluctuations. We recommend changes to timing procedures that leverage instrumentation advances to improve timing precision.

papers.title: A possible connection between the ridge and hypotenuse in the bispectrum of black hole X-ray binaries through quasi-periodic modulation
papers.abstract: Quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in black-hole X-ray binaries show nonlinear coupling with broadband variability, producing characteristic ridge, hypotenuse, and web-like structures in the bicoherence. However, the origin of these structures remains unclear. We develop a mathematical model in which a modulator phase-locked to the QPO acts multiplicatively on the underlying variability. The resulting frequency mixing naturally produces both the ridge and hypotenuse associated with the fundamental QPO, as two parts of the same modulation-induced bispectral structure, and the same mechanism extends to the second harmonic. The model further predicts opposite-sign biphases between each ridge and its corresponding hypotenuse. We test these predictions using NICER observations of Swift~J1727.8$-$1613 and MAXI~J1820$+$070. The bispectral maps show QPO-related ridge--hypotenuse structures broadly consistent with the model, with qualitatively opposite-sign biphases between each ridge and its corresponding hypotenuse. In particular, the biphase map provides a complementary diagnostic that reveals weak coupling structures that are difficult to identify from the bicoherence alone. We also compare the measured bispectral modulus with the predictions for isolated ridges and hypotenuses. These predictions broadly reproduce the observed frequency dependence, while localized deviations remain near the fundamental-QPO and second-harmonic frequencies, where different bispectral structures overlap. Our results provide a simple mathematical framework in which the web-like pattern in the bispectrum could arise naturally from multiplicative coupling between a QPO-phase-locked modulator and the underlying variability.

papers.title: Forecasting Fundamental-Plane Tests of Intermediate-mass Black Holes in Radio-selected Dwarf Galaxies
papers.abstract: A radio/X-ray Fundamental Plane (FP) test of an intermediate-mass black hole is informative only when the compact radio emission, hard X-rays, accretion state, and host association refer to the same accretor. We used published VLA, VLBA, \textit{Chandra}, and \textit{HST} observations of a radio-selected dwarf-galaxy sample to determine when present nondetections are constraining and what observations are required for a stronger test. The VLBA follow-up reveals that compactness alone does not establish association with the target dwarf, while for the best nuclear candidates the radio component relevant to the FP has not yet been isolated on the intermediate physical scales between the VLA and VLBA measurements. We therefore recast the FP as a forward question: for an assumed black-hole mass, how likely is a given radio observation to detect the compact core? The calculation includes intrinsic FP scatter, X-ray uncertainties, the radio spectral index, the accretion state, and source size relative to the beam. The existing VLBA nondetections have low completeness across the adopted intermediate-mass range and do not provide useful black-hole mass upper limits. Meaningful tests require deeper resolution-matched radio imaging, recovery of intermediate-scale structure, and contemporaneous measurements of the intrinsic hard-X-ray component. Because the calculation returns a mass-dependent detection function for each source, the same framework can be applied to larger dwarf-galaxy samples to quantify survey completeness and build selection functions for population studies of low-mass black holes.

papers.title: Superorbital period evolution of Hercules X-1
papers.abstract: Context. Hercules X-1 (Her X-1) is a well-studied X-ray binary exhibiting superorbital modulation of its X-ray flux. The origin of this periodicity remains debated between a counter-precessing twisted-tilted accretion disc and free precession of the neutron star. Earlier observations (1970-1990) reported stochastic fluctuations in the superorbital period, with no long-term trend. Aims. We investigated the long-term trend of the superorbital modulation using more recent, uninterrupted data from 1995-2025 to identify features that may favour or disfavour the proposed mechanisms. Methods. We probed the superorbital period using long-term light curves from five X-ray monitors, namely CGRO/BATSE, RXTE/ASM, Swift/BAT, Fermi/GBM, and MAXI/GSC, together with literature data spanning $\sim$50 yr. We employed multiple timing analysis tools to trace its evolution. Results. The uninterrupted data from the last 30 years show that the superorbital period is decreasing at a rate of $\sim -5 \times 10^{-5}$ s s$^{-1}$. The $O-C$ analysis reveals shorter-timescale variability superimposed on the overall decay; thus, a simple quadratic function cannot explain the observed $O-C$ variations. We also find a positive correlation between the mean count rate and superorbital period across different linear segments of the $O-C$ curve. Conclusions. Period variations over a few to a few tens of superorbital cycles suggest a restoring mechanism in the system. We discuss possible mechanisms responsible for the observed long-term decay and short-term variability. (Abbreviated.)

papers.title: Entanglement in Collective Neutrino Oscillations on a Quantum Computer
papers.abstract: Simulations on a quantum computer have been propounded as a next-generation tool for studying neutrino flavour oscillations in dense environments like supernovae or neutron star mergers. However, quantum advantage hinges on the presence of quantum entanglement in the neutrino ensemble, and it has been argued that such entanglement becomes negligible in the limit of large neutrino number density. Here, we address this question by explicitly simulating the multiparticle dynamics of entangled neutrino ensembles with a varying number of particles, $N$, on both classical and quantum hardware, and comparing our results to those obtained with conventional ``mean-field'' methods based on Boltzmann-type kinetic equations. For simple toy systems, we demonstrate both analytically and numerically that, indeed, the predictions of full multiparticle simulations agree with those of mean-field methods in the large-$N$ limit. Along the way, we develop novel algorithms for the efficient simulation of entangled neutrino gases on both classical and quantum hardware. We then discuss physical situations in which an entangled neutrino system \emph{cannot} be described through mean-field dynamics alone and quantum entanglement therefore becomes phenomenologically relevant. We comment on the conditions under which these scenarios may be realized in supernova cores or neutron star mergers.

papers.title: Phentax: A JAX implementation of the IMRPhenomTHM waveform model
papers.abstract: The upcoming Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) is expected to be sensitive to thousands of white dwarf (WD) binaries in our galaxy, extreme mass ratio inspirals (EMRIs) of stellar-mass compact objects into massive black holes, stellar-mass black hole binaries (SOBHBs) in their early inspiral phase, and, crucially, massive black hole binaries (MBHBs) with masses in the range of $10^4$-$10^7 M_\odot$. The presence of such a large number of signals requires joint inference of all parameters across all sources present in the data, an approach referred to as "global fit". This requires evaluating hundreds of thousands of waveform templates, which can be computationally expensive. To address this challenge, we present $\texttt{Phentax}$, a $\texttt{JAX}$ re-implementation of the $\texttt{IMRPhenomTHM}$ waveform model. This is a state-of-the-art time-domain phenomenological waveform model for comparable-mass binary black holes that includes the effects of higher-order modes. Given this, $\texttt{IMRPhenomTHM}$ is one of the models currently used to simulate and analyze MBHB signals in LISA. With $\texttt{Phentax}$, we provide a fast, easy-to-batch, and differentiable implementation of this waveform model to accelerate the development of LISA global fit algorithms.

papers.title: A pipeline for identifying astrophysical signals and instrumental glitches in LISA data
papers.abstract: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) is a space-based gravitational wave detector scheduled for launch in the 2030s by the European Space Agency. Operating in the 0.1 mHz to 0.1 Hz band, LISA will observe a variety of astrophysical sources including but not limited to supermassive black hole mergers, extreme mass ratio inspirals, and white dwarf binaries. LISA will yield new insights, including supermassive black hole formation, new tests of general relativity, population studies of white dwarfs and others. Like all interferometric gravitational wave detectors, LISA data is expected to contain non-astrophysical transients, commonly referred to as glitches. We introduce a two step pipeline that consists of a search algorithm for detecting potential transients in simulated LISA data followed by a machine learning model that classifies the detected transients as gravitational waves or instrumental glitches. This is important for MBHBs with very high masses (around $10^6\ M_{\odot}$) which are transients that could be morphologically similar to LISA glitches in the data. Initial results demonstrate a promising ability to classify detected events with an accuracy close to $98\%$. The pipeline also shows the ability to analyze a month of data in under 2 minutes on a laptop. This shows an eventual utility of our pipeline for enabling accurate rapid alerts from low latency searches. It could also support model selection in global-fit analyses by providing an initial summary of the location and type of individual signals. This paper also discusses challenges encountered during training, including limitations of the current framework.

papers.title: Baryon Number Susceptibilities of Hot and Dense Nuclear Matter in Relativistic Mean-Field Models
papers.abstract: We develop a fully analytical framework for calculating baryon number susceptibilities in relativistic mean-field (RMF) models of hot and dense nuclear matter at finite temperature and baryon chemical potential. The formalism is applied to representative nonlinear RMF parameterization sets to investigate the model dependence of baryon number fluctuations over a wide range of temperatures and baryon chemical potentials. All the considered RMF parameterizations reproduce the overall qualitative beam-energy dependence of the cumulant ratios. The observed skewness and kurtosis within the RMF models satisfy the experimental values. Specifically, the FSU-family parameterizations exhibit relatively small deviations from the measured heavy-ion observables i.e. cumulant ratios.

papers.title: Probing flavor-dependent neutrino-dark matter interactions with the flavor composition of high-energy cosmic neutrinos
Mathematical foundations and numerical simulations of BDNK hydrodynamics: from heavy-ion collisions to astrophysics
papers.abstract: We present new developments in the mathematical foundations and numerical simulations of the causal and stable first-order relativistic viscous hydrodynamic theory by Bemfica, Disconzi, Noronha, and Kovtun (BDNK) in general spacetimes. We develop two independent flux-conservative algorithms for arbitrary 3+1-dimensional spacetime metrics. Both are hyperbolic, causal, and well-posed, pass convergence tests, and reproduce known results. The first uses a new first-order reduction with mathematically preserved constraints, whose numerical violations can be handled with cleaning fields (the resulting coupled system is proven hyperbolic and well-posed). The second uses a new mixed-order formulation, whose solutions are proven strictly equivalent to the original BDNK system, without cleaning fields. Our proofs rely on a new general theorem providing sufficient conditions for transforming a mixed-order system with arbitrary-order equations into a strictly hyperbolic system, strengthening a classical result by Choquet Bruhat for weak hyperbolicity. We introduce a new practical prescription for selecting admissible hydrodynamic frames for a broad class of equations of state, including nonconformal ones relevant to heavy-ion collisions and astrophysics. Our simulations capture viscous shock broadening and suppression of Kelvin--Helmholtz vortices, reproduce Bjorken and Gubser flows, and study departures from stationary ideal-fluid configurations in Michel accretion and rotating tori on fixed Schwarzschild and Kerr backgrounds. For heavy-ion collisions, we perform boost invariant simulations with a lattice-QCD-based equation of state and fluctuating TRENTo initial conditions, comparing BDNK with a minimal Israel--Stewart theory. The descriptions agree at small shear viscosity but can differ substantially at larger viscosities, particularly for early initialization with rapid longitudinal expansion.

papers.title: Tidal Deformability of Neutron Stars in Scalar-Tensor Theories of Gravity
papers.abstract: Gravitational waves from compact binary coalescences are valuable for testing theories of gravity in the strong field regime. By measuring neutron star tidal deformability using gravitational waves from binary neutron stars, stringent constraints were placed on the equation of state of matter at extreme densities. Tidal Love numbers in alternative theories of gravity may differ significantly from their general relativistic counterparts. Understanding exactly how the tidal Love numbers change will enable scientists to untangle physics beyond general relativity from the uncertainty in the equation of state measurement. In this work, we explicitly calculate the fully relativistic $l \geq 2$ tidal love numbers for neutron stars in scalar-tensor theories of gravitation. We use several realistic equations of state to explore how the mass, radius, and tidal deformability relations differ from those of general relativity. We find that tidal Love numbers and tidal deformabilities can differ significantly from those in general relativity in certain regimes. The electric tidal deformability can differ by $\sim 200\%$, and the magnetic tidal deformability differs by $\sim 300 \%$. These deviations occur at large compactnesses ($C = M/r \gtrsim 0.2$) and vary slightly depending on the equation of state. This difference suggests that using the tidal Love numbers from general relativity could lead to significant errors in tests of general relativity using the gravitational waves from binary neutron star and neutron-star--black-hole mergers.

papers.title: Challenging the Weak Cosmic Censorship with Phantom Fields
papers.abstract: Penrose's weak cosmic censorship conjecture asserts that spacetime singularities produced by gravitational collapse are generically hidden behind event horizons, thus preventing them from causally influencing distant observers and preserving the predictability of the exterior region. In this work, we probe this conjecture in a setup that deliberately violates one of its central assumptions - the dominant energy condition - by considering the spherical collapse of a phantom scalar field with negative energy density. In principle, such a field could produce a Schwarzschild geometry with negative mass and therefore no event horizon. Our aim is to assess whether, once the dominant energy condition is abandoned, the fully coupled evolution of matter and geometry can dynamically generate or expose naked singularities, thereby probing the robustness of cosmic censorship. To this end, we perform high-accuracy numerical relativity simulations based on fourth-order finite-difference schemes. Starting from smooth, asymptotically flat initial data representing regular phantom scalar wave packets, we follow their fully nonlinear evolution through collapse or dispersion. While an ordinary (positive-energy) scalar field exhibits the standard Choptuik critical behavior at the threshold of black-hole formation, the phantom field displays qualitatively different dynamics. For all amplitudes considered, we find no evidence for trapped surfaces, naked singularities, or alternative stationary end states. Instead, the phantom scalar field disperses in all the configurations studied. Within the parameter space explored, we find no dynamical violation of cosmic censorship.

papers.title: Relativistic mode sums for neutron-star tidal response
papers.abstract: Time-dependent tidal interactions during the late inspiral of binary neutron stars encode valuable information about neutron-star structure, but systematically extending the familiar Newtonian mode-sum picture into full general relativity is nontrivial. In this paper, we develop a practical relativistic implementation of mode-sum tidal response for non-rotating neutron stars in Regge-Wheeler gauge. Using near-zone boundary conditions, we systematically define the interior tidal field, the relativistic overlap integrals, and the corresponding mode amplitudes. The good is that the dominant f-mode contribution is remarkably robust, reproducing the direct matching calculation to within $\sim 3$\% across the equations of state we consider. The bad is that the operator governing mode inner product is not positive definite on the full Regge-Wheeler-gauge function space, so the relativistic mode sum truncated at ${\cal{O}}(\omega^2)$ is not expected to strictly converge to the direct matching solution. The subtle is that the tidal field inside the star is not unique, although this ambiguity has only a limited impact on the dominant f-mode response for the classes of extensions studied here. Our results establish the practical utility of relativistic mode-sum approximations, while making clear that their predictive power comes from a controlled low-mode description, rather than from a formally convergent strong-field expansion.

papers.title: New Universal Relations for Magnetized Neutron Stars
papers.abstract: Unlike the neutron-star mass--radius relation, which depends sensitively on the internal stellar structure through the equation of state of dense nuclear matter, certain neutron-star properties obey approximately universal relations that exhibit only weak dependence on the equation of state. In this paper, we explore new universal relations for magnetized neutron stars. We focus on a purely poloidal dipolar magnetic-field configuration and treat the effects of the magnetic field perturbatively to second order in the field strength. After appropriately normalizing the relevant quantities by the stellar mass and the magnetic-field strength at the pole, we first identify an exact universal relation between the magnetic dipole moment and stellar compactness. We then find approximate universal relations among the magnetic dipole moment, magnetically-induced stellar quadrupole moment, and ellipticity, with fractional variations due to the equation of state at the level of O(10%). We support these numerical findings with analytic estimates for Newtonian polytropes, which reproduce the observed behavior. Among the newly discovered relations, the one connecting the magnetic dipole moment and stellar quadrupole moment may be particularly useful for the analysis of gravitational-wave signals from binaries containing magnetized neutron stars.

papers.title: On the nature of oscillating modes of proto-neutron stars
papers.abstract: Newborn proto-neutron stars (PNS) are potential targets of gravitational wave asteroseismology, the study of the (inner) structure of stars via their oscillation modes. To prepare for the eventual detection of such modes by current and future gravitational wave observatories, theoretical studies have obtained the possible spectrum of oscillations. However, there has been disagreement when it comes to identifying and classifying specific modes according to the physical mechanism that excites them. In this paper, we present a novel scheme to classify the oscillation modes of a newly born PNS surrounded by a stalled accretion shock in core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe). Our classification is physically motivated, as it is based on the energy of the restoring forces of the mode. We investigate the nature of the modes by considering the different regions of the CCSN that they stem from. We apply this scheme to a set of 28 non-rotating 1D, 2D and 3D CCSN simulations performed with two different numerical codes and using different progenitors and equations of state. In that way, we find that there are different families of f-, p- and g-modes in the system, living in different areas. More specifically, we identify two families of f- and p-modes associated with the PNS and the shock, respectively, and two families of g-modes originating from the two convectively stable regions, one in the PNS core and one near its surface. We also find that the dominant high-frequency emission mode is the f-mode of the PNS, associated with the strong density gradient at its surface. Our classification procedure is automatic, performs consistently for all the models considered, and paves the way to systematic studies of the dependence of the mode frequencies on the PNS properties, with direct application to parameter estimation from future observations of gravitational wave signals.
